_comment: Byte-for-byte copies of FamCart modules. Vendored rather than imported because
this repo is a submodule and must also work as a standalone clone, where
../../src/... does not exist. Same arrangement the catalog importer uses.
What is vendored here is the DESIGN SYSTEM, not logic. style.css carries the
whole token set and both themes; theme.ts carries the one storage key and the
one resolver that stamps data-theme onto the root element. The admin tool has
to look like the same product and remember the same preference, and the only
way to guarantee that across two repos is to copy the files and then refuse to
let the copies drift.
sha256 is authoritative: FamCart's test/vendorDrift.test.js reads this file and
compares both copies, so an edit to either side fails a test at the moment it
is made. Never edit these files directly -- change the upstream module and
re-copy, then update the hash.
The hash is of the LF-NORMALIZED bytes. FamCart is developed on Windows with
core.autocrlf=true, so the working copy is CRLF there and LF on a Linux CI
runner; hashing the raw file would make this test pass on one and fail on the
other.
Refresh with, from the FamCart root:
cp src/style.css admin/src/vendor/style.css
tr -d '\r' < src/style.css | sha256sum
public/fonts/*.woff2 are copied alongside these and deliberately NOT hashed
here: they are binary assets that change only when the typeface does, and the
@font-face rules inside style.css already fail loudly if they go missing.

style.css.why: The token set and both themes. A divergent copy means the admin tool drifts away from the product it is reporting on, one colour at a time.

theme.ts.why: Same storage key, same modes, same resolver. Vendoring it is what makes the dark-mode preference one setting rather than two that happen to agree.
